title: Public Peeks — the stated core differentiator — are gated off in every production configuration path in the repository and release acceptance is unevidenced
evidence: featureFlags.js:25 tours: stagingCertifiedFlag('VITE_FEATURE_TOURS'); App.jsx:171 route /peek rendered only when (tours || toursPreview); ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md:27 'True only for an accepted Peek release'; TOURS_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md:13 'in staging only'
impact: With the flag false the /peek route does not exist, so Public Peek discovery is absent from production. A product defined by Peeks would launch without them.
reproduction: Build with VITE_FEATURE_TOURS unset and navigate to /peek — PageNotFound
root_cause: Deliberate release gate pending Peek release acceptance; not a code defect
recommended_fix: Complete and evidence Peek release acceptance per docs/TOURS_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md, then set the production flag; or make an explicit documented decision to launch without Public Peeks
test_to_prove_fix: Hosted check that /peek returns the Peek catalogue on the production origin
notes: Remedy is release acceptance not a code fix. Severity reflects launch-definition impact

title: Capability gating trusts a client-readable hostname prefix
evidence: STAGING_HOST_PREFIX='findit-marketplace-stagi'; isTrustedStagingHost() reads globalThis.location.hostname; resolveStagingCertifiedFlag returns isTrustedStagingEnvironment(env) || readBooleanFlag(...)
impact: Any deployment served from a hostname matching findit-marketplace-stagi*.vercel.app auto-enables messaging, notifications, Peeks and current-location regardless of build-time env. Trust decision is made from browser-visible state rather than build-time configuration.
reproduction: Serve the production bundle from a matching hostname; gated flags turn on
root_cause: Runtime hostname used as an authorization-adjacent trust signal
recommended_fix: Decide capabilities at build time from env only; drop the hostname branch
test_to_prove_fix: Unit test asserting isTrustedStagingEnvironment ignores location.hostname
notes: Impact is capability exposure not auth bypass

evidence: Step 10 'Verify SQL migration boundary' fails; steps 11,13,14,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,23,24 all report conclusion=skipped, including 'Lint application', 'Typecheck application', 'Typecheck active release surface', 'Build production application', 'Run all contracts' and 'Run reproducible internal certification'. title: Permissions-Policy camera=() may conflict with Peek capture, and UI copy anticipates a permission the capture flow never requests
evidence: vercel.json:29 'camera=()' is an empty allowlist disabling camera for all origins including self. src/ contains no getUserMedia or MediaRecorder; capture uses TourUploader.jsx:211 <input type=file accept=video/* capture=environment>, which delegates to the OS camera app and is generally not governed by this directive.
impact: If any browser does gate <input capture> on the camera policy, seller Peek capture breaks in production with no fallback signalled. Independently, TourUploader.jsx:129 and CameraPermissionDialog tell users to grant a browser camera permission that this flow never requests, which will misdirect anyone who hits a capture failure.
reproduction: Open the Peek capture flow on a real iOS and Android device against a deployment serving this header
root_cause: Header written for a getUserMedia design; implementation uses the native picker instead
recommended_fix: Verify on real devices; set camera=(self) if capture is gated, and correct the permission copy to match the native-picker flow
test_to_prove_fix: Real-device test of seller Peek capture on iOS Safari and Android Chrome against production headers
notes: Downgraded from an initial P1 read after confirming no getUserMedia usage

title: Post-deploy chunk-load rejection surfaces as a generic error screen rather than a reload prompt
evidence: Suspense at App.jsx:154 handles pending lazy imports but not rejected ones. AppErrorBoundary (main.jsx:43-45) catches the throw, so there is no white screen, but it renders a generic error rather than prompting the reload that actually fixes a rotated chunk manifest.
impact: A user with an open tab during a deploy sees an unexplained error screen. Cache-Control no-store on HTML plus immutable on /assets/* means a manual reload does recover, so impact is confusion rather than a stuck app.
reproduction: Deploy, then trigger a lazy route in a tab opened before the deploy
root_cause: Chunk-load rejection not distinguished from generic render errors
recommended_fix: Detect ChunkLoadError / dynamic import failure in AppErrorBoundary and offer reload
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a simulated dynamic-import rejection renders the reload affordance
notes: Error boundary coverage itself is good

title: PWA manifest ships a single SVG icon with no apple-touch-icon, no raster PNG and no maskable purpose, and a contract test locks it in
evidence: manifest icons array contains exactly one entry, /brand/peekalisting-binoculars.svg, sizes 'any', purpose 'any'. index.html declares rel=icon and rel=mask-icon but no rel=apple-touch-icon. The test asserts manifest.icons.every(icon => icon.src === '/brand/peekalisting-binoculars.svg').
impact: iOS ignores the manifest for home-screen icons and needs a PNG apple-touch-icon, so Add to Home Screen yields a blank or screenshot icon on iPhone and iPad. Android adaptive masking crops or letterboxes the mark and the splash screen has no raster source. The product is mobile-first and actively prompts installation, so this hits the primary install path. The contract test would fail any correct fix.
reproduction: Add to Home Screen on iOS Safari; inspect the installed icon
root_cause: Icon set reduced to a single SVG during the rebrand and then frozen by a test assertion
recommended_fix: Add 180px apple-touch-icon plus 192/512 PNG icons and a maskable variant, all PeekaListing-branded; relax the test to assert brand correctness rather than an exact single-source icon list
test_to_prove_fix: Manifest test asserting presence of 192/512 raster icons and a maskable purpose, plus an apple-touch-icon link in index.html
notes: public/brand/findit-icon-180.png is the right size but off-brand and unreferenced
